source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Maize dwarf mosaic virus (ជម្ងឺគៀលក្រៀម, Maize Dwarf Mosaic Virus): symptoms are especially recognized by mottled/mosaic patterning and stunting. Symptoms of this disease commonly appear at the seedling stage, before flowering; once infected, the plant's leaves become yellowed and growth is stunted from that point onward.

This disease cannot be cured once the plant is infected -- there is no treatment to reverse infection, and the virus continues to affect the corn plant's growth. It spreads readily by insect vectors, specifically aphids, notably the green peach aphid (Green Peach Aphid). This is a viral disease and there is no direct chemical cure for the virus itself.

Prevention and control measures include:
- Select and use clean seed that carries no history of the disease.
- Use resistant/tolerant varieties.
- Sanitize tools used in the field.
- Time planting appropriately, to avoid periods of heavy aphid/vector pressure or when conditions favor vector population buildup.
- Remove and destroy infected plants, and uproot plants showing virus symptoms and dispose of them away from the field.
